title: Mousambi (Sweet Lime): modeled ₹623/qtl left, Una → Kangra (Baijnath)
summary: January 2024: reported mousambi (Sweet Lime) prices at Una and Kangra (Baijnath) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 80% of 20 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹623 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 14 same-variety market pairs screened for mousambi (Sweet Lime) in January 2024; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Mousambi, Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kangra (Baijnath) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2024
scenes.caption: Una (Himachal Pradesh) and Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported mousambi (Sweet Lime) prices for the same variety and grade (Mousambi, Medium) on 20 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Una reported a median ₹4,625 per quintal. Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹5,550 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,050/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,050 per quintal, and Kangra (Baijnath) was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 93 km by road
scenes.caption: 93 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~2 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹20/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹506 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹221 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kangra (Baijnath) report, the rule selects 15 of 20 modeled shipping days. 14 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹623 per quintal (₹330 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Mousambi (Sweet Lime) route from Una to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 80% of matched days in January 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹62,300, or ₹33,000 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to mousambi (Sweet Lime)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹20/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Mousambi (Sweet Lime) route from Una to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 80% of matched days in January 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹62,300, or ₹33,000 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

title: Mousambi (Sweet Lime): modeled ₹647/qtl left, Una → Kangra (Baijnath)
summary: December 2024: reported mousambi (Sweet Lime) prices at Una and Kangra (Baijnath) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 78% of 23 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹647 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 14 same-variety market pairs screened for mousambi (Sweet Lime) in December 2024; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Mousambi, Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kangra (Baijnath) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.
